project.name: Doshomik
project.source: the SQL migrations in `apps/api/migrations/` (read from a database migrated with all seven)

areas.name: Accounts and sign-in
areas.desc: Who people are, their devices, outside sign-ins and one-time email codes.

areas.name: Media
areas.desc: Every uploaded image or video, whatever it is used for.

areas.name: Posts, comments and notifications
areas.desc: The feed: posts, likes, saves, comment threads and the notifications they cause.

areas.name: Learn
areas.desc: Topics (concepts), learn items, courses and what each user has completed.

areas.name: Practice
areas.desc: Questions, quizzes and every answer a user gives.

areas.name: Research
areas.desc: The curated paper collection, Paper Cards, lineage, Learn first, saves, the reading tracker, roadmaps and trails.

areas.name: System
areas.desc: The worker's job queue and the audit trail.

columns.public_id: Exposed as `id` in the API. The numeric `id` never leaves the server
columns.username: Also unique on `lower(username)`. Pattern `^[a-z0-9_.]{3,30}$` is enforced in the app
columns.avatar_url: Set by the worker when an avatar upload is ready
columns.is_private: Private accounts need accepted follow requests
columns.totp_enabled_at: Two-factor sign-in is on. Required for staff routes
columns.follower_count: Stored count of **accepted** follows. Moved ±1 by the worker on `follow.changed`; repaired hourly
columns.following_count: Stored count of **accepted** follows. Moved ±1 by the worker on `follow.changed`; repaired hourly

notes: Deleting a user removes their posts, likes, saves, follows, blocks, sessions, progress, attempts, notifications, reading passes, saved outputs and trails.
Their comments, reports, media ownership, audit entries and `created_by` / `updated_by` are set to NULL instead, so threads and history survive.

columns.public_id: The `sid` claim in access tokens; the first part of the refresh token
columns.refresh_token_hash: SHA-256 of the secret part; replaced on every refresh
columns.app_version: `dev-bypass` marks the long-lived sessions made by the development auth bypass

notes: Expired or revoked sessions are deleted 30 days later by the hourly clean-up.

auth_identities.purpose: One row per outside sign-in (Google, later Apple) linked to an account.

auth_tokens.purpose: One row per one-time email code.

columns.token_hash: The plain code is only in the email

notes: Expired or used codes are deleted 7 days later.

follows.purpose: One row per follower and followed pair, kept for ever and toggled.

columns.status: accepted · pending (a request to a private account) · inactive (unfollowed, withdrawn, declined, or ended by a block)
columns.updated_at: When the current status began. Follow requests are listed by it

notes: A toggle row: unfollowing sets `inactive` instead of deleting, so only the first follow ever notifies.
The API reports `inactive` as `follow_status: "none"`. Every privacy check tests `status = 'accepted'`.

blocks.purpose: One row per user who has blocked another, kept after an unblock.

columns.created_at: The first block; kept when blocking again
columns.is_active: false after an unblock; blocking again sets it back

notes: Applies both ways in every visibility check.
A toggle row: unblocking sets `is_active = false` instead of deleting. Only active rows count; every check filters on `is_active`.
Blocking also sets follows in both directions to `inactive`.

reports.purpose: One row per report of a user, post, comment or trail.

columns.target_id: Internal id of the row named by `target_type`. No foreign key on purpose: the report outlives its target

notes: Resolving a report can dismiss it, remove the content, or suspend the responsible user.
The API checks that the target exists in the table `target_type` names, and that the reporter may see it, before filing a report.

media_assets.purpose: One row per uploaded image or video.

columns.provider: `self` (FFmpeg worker) or `legacy` (Prototype 1 files); later a managed provider
columns.raw_key: Original upload in private raw storage. Deleted after processing, success or failure
columns.playback_key: HLS master playlist (video) or base key of the WebP variants (image)
columns.duration_ms: Measured by the worker, never taken from the client. Reels are capped at 90 s here, not in a CHECK
columns.error: Message shown to the user when `failed`

notes: Stores storage keys, not URLs. URLs are built at read time, so changing storage provider changes no data.
Rows with `status = 'processing'` are the worker's media queue.
Abandoned `uploading` or `failed` assets older than 1 day, used by no post or learn item, are deleted hourly.

posts.purpose: One row per post: text, one image, or one reel.

columns.caption: Required for `text` posts
columns.media_id: Required unless `type = 'text'`. The asset can't be deleted while a post uses it
columns.status: processing (media not ready) · published · removed (by a moderator)
columns.like_count: Stored counter, moved ±1 by the worker
columns.comment_count: Stored counter, moved ±1 by the worker
columns.deleted_at: Hidden at once; the row and its media are purged after 30 days
columns.topic_id: Optional concept tag, so a reel can be the link of a paper's Learn first topic

post_likes.purpose: One row per user and post, kept for ever and toggled.

columns.is_active: `false` after an unlike; a re-like sets it back. Deliberately in no index

notes: A toggle row: only the first like ever sends a notification.
Because `is_active` is in no index, a toggle is a HOT update with no index writes.

saved_posts.purpose: One row per post a user bookmarked.
notes: Plain delete and insert on purpose: no side effects, and a re-save must move the post to the top.

comments.purpose: One row per comment or reply, on a post or in a paper's discussion.

columns.user_id: NULL once the author's account is purged; the thread survives
columns.post_id: Exactly one of `post_id` and `paper_id` is set
columns.paper_id: The paper's discussion thread. Shares reports, blocks, rate limits and moderation with post comments
columns.parent_id: The comment this one replies to

notes: No `updated_at`: comments are not edited.

notifications.purpose: One row per notification shown to a user.
notes: Written only by the worker, from outbox events.

topics.purpose: One row per concept: the unit that links lessons, quizzes, reels and paper prerequisites.

columns.summary: Shown in Learn first when the topic has no learn items yet

learn_items.purpose: One row per short video, figure or text explanation.

columns.media_url: An outside link. Either this or `media_id` is needed unless `kind = 'text'`
columns.media_id: Uploaded media. The asset can't be deleted while an item uses it

courses.purpose: One row per course: an ordered set of learn items, or a card linking to a free outside course.

columns.external_url: Set for an outside course, which has no items

course_items.purpose: One row per step of a course.
notes: The primary key is deferrable, so a whole course can be reordered in one transaction.
Steps are renumbered 1..n over the **published** items in the API.

course_progress.purpose: One row per user and course they started.
notes: Written with one upsert, which also marks the steps reached in [[learn_item_completions]].

learn_item_completions.purpose: One row per learn item a user completed, wherever they opened it.
notes: Feeds "done" in Learn before reading.

user_known_topics.purpose: One row per topic a user marked "I already know this".
notes: The spec's `user_known_concepts`. Counts every Learn first link of that topic as done.
No `created_at` (inherited from Prototype 1).

question_attempts.purpose: One row per answer a user gave.
notes: Append-only history. Powers accuracy per topic, streak days (in `APP_TIMEZONE`) and "quiz done" in Learn before reading.

quizzes.purpose: One row per named set of questions in a fixed order.
notes: Has no `published_at` or `updated_by`, unlike the other team content.

quiz_questions.purpose: One row per question in a quiz, at its position.

fields.purpose: One row per research field, shown as a chip on the Research tab.
notes: Can't be deleted while it has papers.

papers.purpose: One row per paper in the curated collection.

columns.title: Empty for an import until the first sync
columns.paper_url: The original's abstract page: the main **Open** action. We never host a PDF
columns.code_url: Linked code repository from Hugging Face
columns.search_vector: Title, authors, and the questions and key idea of both Paper Cards. Built only by `refresh_paper_search(paper_id)`

notes: Ingested fields are written only by the worker. Descriptive fields are filled only when empty, so staff edits win.
The app never calls a scholarly API; requests read only this table and its neighbours.

Its outside ids, metrics and ingestion state are in three one-to-one tables created with it: [[paper_metadata]], [[paper_metrics]] and [[paper_sync]]. Its structured explanation is in [[paper_cards]].

paper_metadata.purpose: One row per paper: its outside identifiers and what OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar say about it.

columns.paper_id: Also the primary key: one row per paper, deleted with it
columns.openalex_topics: `[{id, name, score}]`, for staff choosing the field

notes: Each id is unique: importing or editing a paper with an id already in the collection answers `409`.
The worker matches references against these ids to build [[paper_edges]].

paper_metrics.purpose: One row per paper: how popular it is and its place in the default Research order.

columns.paper_id: Also the primary key: one row per paper, deleted with it
columns.citation_count: Semantic Scholar, else OpenAlex. Refreshed every sync
columns.hf_trending_at: The last day the paper was on Hugging Face daily papers
columns.trend_rank: 1..n over published papers: the default order. Recomputed hourly and after each sync. NULL = not ranked (drafts, archived, or not ranked yet), sorted last

notes: Written only by the worker. Lists join it for every paper they show.

paper_sync.purpose: One row per paper: its place in the ingestion queue.

columns.paper_id: Also the primary key: one row per paper, deleted with it
columns.sync_error: The last ingestion error; NULL after a clean sync

notes: Only papers with a DOI or arXiv id in [[paper_metadata]] are picked. Each is refreshed every 7 days; **Sync now** sets `synced_at` back to NULL.

paper_cards.purpose: One row per paper and language: its Paper Card.

columns.question: Searched, in both languages
columns.extra_questions: Further research questions, in order. Searched
columns.data_source: The data or benchmarks the paper uses
columns.figures: `[{url, caption}]`. Images are uploads with purpose `paper_figure`

notes: The only home of a paper's structured explanation. The Prototype 2 summary fields of the paper APIs (`research_questions`, `main_idea`, `results`…) read and write the English card.
Migration 006 moved the old summary columns of [[papers]] here. Where a card and the old summary disagreed, the losing text is in [[audit_log]] (action `paper.summary_migration`).

paper_edges.purpose: One row per citation between two papers in the collection.

columns.intent: background · supporting · contrasting. NULL = unknown. `contrasting` is set only by staff
columns.s2_intents: Semantic Scholar's own labels, kept as they came

notes: Built from each paper's own references. The worker never changes a staff edge's intent.

paper_prerequisites.purpose: One row per concept to learn before reading a paper (Learn first).

columns.label: Shown instead of the topic name when set
columns.why: One line on why it is needed
columns.learn_item_id: At most one of the three links is set
columns.quiz_id: At most one of the three links is set
columns.reel_post_id: At most one of the three links is set
columns.suggested_by: staff · ai. Any `ai` row shows the disclosure footnote

notes: "Done" is always computed, never stored.

paper_saves.purpose: One row per paper a user bookmarked.

columns.created_at: Orders Saved and picks Up next

reading_passes.purpose: One row per user and paper they started reading: the three-step tracker.

columns.note: Private, at most 400 characters. Returned only to its owner

notes: Steps are cumulative: setting step 3 also stamps steps 1 and 2.
Lowering the step clears the later times, so monthly counts never include a step the user took back.

research_outputs.purpose: One row per saved result of a Research tool (map, roadmap, comparison, claim check).
notes: Reopening one reads the stored `result`: no AI call. Nothing writes these rows yet (Group C).

trails.purpose: One row per reading path a user made.
notes: Publishing needs at least 2 papers.
A published trail follows its author's visibility like a post, and can be reported.

trail_items.purpose: One row per paper in a trail, at its position.

columns.note: One line per step, at most 280 characters

roadmap_steps.purpose: One row per paper in a field's starting roadmap, made by the team.

columns.note: Why the paper comes at that point

user_papers.purpose: One row per user and paper in the old Prototype 2 tracker.
notes: Superseded by [[paper_saves]] and [[reading_passes]], which were backfilled from it.
Writes to the old endpoints don't reach the new tables. Drop it once no client calls `/papers/:id/status`.

user_fields.purpose: One row per field a user picked as an interest at onboarding.
notes: Saving writes only the difference.

outbox_events.purpose: One row per piece of work for the background worker, written in the same transaction as the change.

columns.entity_id: Internal id of the row named by `entity_type`. No foreign key on purpose: the event outlives its target
columns.attempts: Events failing 10 times stay unprocessed for inspection
columns.processed_at: The worker claims an event by setting this only while it is still NULL

notes: Each event is applied exactly once, so stored counters can move by ±1.
Processed events are deleted after 30 days.

audit_log.purpose: One row per admin or security action.

columns.entity_id: Internal id of the row named by `entity_type`. No foreign key on purpose: the entry outlives its target

badges.toggle row: One row per pair for ever. Its state flips instead of being deleted and re-inserted, so only the first activation notifies.

indexes.posts_user_feed_idx: Profile pages and home feed (keyset on `created_at, id`)
indexes.posts_user_id_created_at_idx: A user's posts in any status; the user cascade
indexes.posts_media_id_idx: Posts waiting on a media asset
indexes.posts_to_tsvector_idx: Full-text search on captions. The query must match the expression exactly
indexes.users_suggest_idx: People to follow, in index order
indexes.follows_following_id_idx: Who follows me; the user cascade
indexes.blocks_blocked_id_idx: Block checks from the blocked side
indexes.post_likes_post_id_idx: Likes per post: the repair job and the post cascade
indexes.notifications_unread_idx: The unread badge on every app open. The query writes `NOT n.is_read` to match it
indexes.paper_metrics_trend_idx: The Research list in trend order (keyset page). Replaces `papers_trend_idx`
indexes.paper_sync_due_idx: Papers due for ingestion, never-synced first. Replaces `papers_sync_idx`
indexes.learn_items_to_tsvector_idx: Full-text search on title and body
indexes.courses_to_tsvector_idx: Full-text search on title and description
indexes.paper_edges_cited_idx: "Built on by": papers citing this one
indexes.research_outputs_user_idx: A user's saved outputs, newest first
indexes.auth_identities_user_id_idx: Lookups and the cascade by user
indexes.auth_tokens_user_id_idx: Lookups and the cascade by user
indexes.reports_target_type_target_id_idx: Earlier reports of the same target

checks.comments_check: A comment is on exactly one of a post or a paper
checks.posts_check: A text post has a caption
checks.posts_media_check: An image or reel post has media
checks.learn_items_check: A video or image item has media (link or upload)
checks.questions_check: An MCQ has at least 2 options
checks.paper_prerequisites_one_link: At most one link per prerequisite
checks.reading_passes_check: Explored time is set exactly while step ≥ 1
checks.reading_passes_check1: Studied time is set exactly while step ≥ 2
checks.reading_passes_check2: Reproduced time is set exactly while step ≥ 3
checks.trail_items_note_check: Step notes are at most 280 characters

highlight.label: new
highlight.note: Added for the Research tab (Group A) in migration `…005`, or by the database refactoring in `…006`.

tour.title: Doshomik in {tables} tables
text: Doshomik Bytes is a bilingual social-learning app for ML, AI and research. One PostgreSQL database holds everything.
The tables fall into {areas} areas, joined by {links} links.

tour.title: Two ids on every row a client can name
text: `id` is a `bigint` used for joins only. It is **never sent to clients**.
`public_id` is a random UUID, sent as `id` in the API. Topics and fields are named by `slug` instead.

tour.title: What happens when something is deleted
text: Every link says what happens to a row when the row it points to is deleted.

visual.cascade: A user's posts, likes, sessions and progress go with them. {cascade} links work this way.
visual.setnull: Comments, reports, media ownership and `created_by` survive with the link cleared. {setnull} links work this way.
visual.restrict: A media asset used by a post, or a field that has papers, can't be deleted: the API answers `409 IN_USE`. {restrict} links work this way.

tour.title: Users are the hub
text: {inFrom:users} tables point at [[users]]. Most of them are what a user owns or did.
An account is soft-deleted first: `status = 'deleted'` hides it at once, and the hourly job purges it after 30 days.

tour.title: Follows and likes are toggled, never re-created
text: A follow or like keeps one row per pair for ever. Unfollowing sets `status = 'inactive'`; unliking sets `is_active = false`.
So only the first follow or like ever sends a notification.

tour.title: Uploads go through media_assets
text: Every image or video is a [[media_assets]] row. The worker checks it, transcodes it and marks it ready.
A post with media waits in `processing` until its asset is ready, then goes live.

tour.title: The worker does the slow work
text: Every change that needs follow-up writes an [[outbox_events]] row in the same transaction.
The worker applies each event exactly once: counters move by ±1, notifications are written, push and email are sent.

tour.title: Team content is drafted, then published
text: Papers, courses, learn items, questions and quizzes start as drafts. Only published rows reach the app.
`created_by` and `updated_by` credit the staff member, and [[audit_log]] records every admin action.

tour.title: Topics tie Learn, Practice and Research together
text: A topic is a concept. Learn items, questions and quizzes are tagged with one.
A paper's Learn first list is a set of topics, so a new video for a topic shows up in every paper that needs it.

tour.title: The research collection
text: Staff import a paper by arXiv id or DOI. The worker fills its metadata from OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and Hugging Face, and ranks the list.
Each paper has a Paper Card per language, and citation lineage to other papers in the collection.
Outside ids, metrics and the ingestion queue sit in three one-to-one tables beside [[papers]], so each changes on its own schedule.

tour.title: What a reader keeps
text: Saving a paper is a [[paper_saves]] row. Reading progress is a separate [[reading_passes]] row with three steps.
Users can also build trails: ordered reading paths others can follow.

tour.title: Where to go next
text: Explore every table and link, or read the reference pages on conventions, retention and migrations.

reference.title: Conventions
reference.desc: Ids, value lists, counters and ordering, the same in every table

items.title: Value lists are CHECKs, not enums
items.text: Status-like columns are `text` with `CHECK (… IN (…))`, which is easier to change in a migration. The same lists live in `packages/shared/src/index.ts`, so change both together.

items.title: Timestamps
items.text: Always `timestamptz`. `updated_at` is set by the application, not by triggers.

items.title: Soft delete
items.text: `deleted_at` hides a row at once; the hourly job purges it later.

items.title: Stored counters
items.text: Moved ±1 by the worker, exactly once per outbox event, and recounted hourly by the repair job.

items.title: Ordered children
items.text: `position` is in the primary key and deferrable, so a whole list can be reordered in one transaction.

items.title: One-to-one companion tables
items.text: `paper_id` is both primary key and foreign key, with `ON DELETE CASCADE`. The API creates all three with the paper, so lists can use inner joins.

items.title: References with no foreign key
items.text: `reports.target_id`, `outbox_events.entity_id` and `audit_log.entity_id` have no foreign key on purpose: these rows must outlive their targets.

items.title: Search expressions must match the indexes
items.text: The full-text expressions in `apps/api/src/db/search.ts` must match the index expressions exactly, or Postgres won't use the indexes. The same goes for partial-index predicates.

sections.title: What is cleaned up, and when

head: Data
Rule
rows: After 30 days: comments blanked to `[deleted]`, the user row deleted (cascading), their media removed
Hidden at once; row and media deleted after 30 days
`uploading` or `failed`, older than 1 day, used by nothing
Expired or revoked more than 30 days ago
Expired or used more than 7 days ago
Processed more than 30 days ago. Events with 10 failed attempts stay for inspection
Deleted as soon as processing ends

head: Database error
API answer
rows: CHECK, NOT NULL or bad format

reference.title: Migrations
reference.desc: The seven SQL files and the rules for adding more

head: File
What it does
rows: The Prototype 1 schema: 16 tables, `pg_trgm`, search indexes
The Prototype 2 appendix: public ids, slugs, media, publishing, auth, safety, outbox and audit
Slugs `NOT NULL`; post media moved into `media_assets`
Session public ids, two-factor columns, four indexes
Toggle rows for likes and follows, stored follow counts
Research tab Group A: 9 new tables, paper metadata and search
Block toggle rows; papers split into `paper_metadata`, `paper_metrics` and `paper_sync`; the old summary moved into `paper_cards`; search rebuilt from the cards

items.title: Never edit an applied migration
items.text: Add a new one. The checklist is in `.claude/skills/doshomik-migration`.

items.title: Every migration has a working down
Regenerate types after a change
items.text: Run `pnpm db:types`, and update `packages/shared` if a value list changed.
